category: free video hosting and HLS streaming host (ad-free), player-embed model

free_tier.stated: "Free and unlimited storage - Stream all your videos freely; we offer endless bandwidth at no charge, and your videos never expire." Also ad-free for free users, and "Unlimited uploads: No limits on size or length."
free_tier.notes: The strongest free claim and the least independently verifiable: three separate unlimiteds (storage, bandwidth, file size) on one page.

per_object_cap.stated: "Unrestricted video uploads: No limits on size or length."
per_object_cap.notes: Recorded as the vendor's claim. No upload was attempted, so a hidden limit above a few GB would not have been seen.

retention.notes: No inactivity clause is printed, unlike every other video host in this set.

egress.terms: "we offer endless bandwidth at no charge". Streaming is HLS, with 'Stream in 4K Ultra HD ... up to 2160p at 60 frames per second' and optional HLS encryption.

interface_detail: The page read describes the player, the upload form and embedding only. No API, FTP or CLI is mentioned on the homepage; the premium page path /premium returns 404, so the paid tier's terms were not read.
tooling: Browser upload and an embed code. No API was found, which for a user is a tooling note and not a verdict: the page's own HTTP endpoints would have to be reversed or driven by a browser session.
chaining: An egress surface rather than a retrieval one: it takes the client's 500 GB-1 TB a day of served video off a paid CDN and puts it on a free host that monetises somewhere else. It pairs with a downloader front end that never touches the bytes.

limits.value: unstated; no rate, connection or daily-volume limit is published

limits_note: Three unlimited claims and no numbers at all. The only premium figure is the paid tier's '10 TB of bandwidth and storage for a simple EUR 10/month', which is smaller than the free tier claims, so the free tier is not a trial of the paid one.
binding_note: No counter is published, so no counter can be named as binding; That is a reliability risk, recorded as such, not a byte limit.

identity_cost.detail: An account is implied by 'your videos' and the upload flow; the signup form was not read, so the exact gate (email versus OAuth) is unverified.

reliability_note: The economics do not add up on the page: unlimited free bandwidth with no ads and no expiry is funded by something the site does not disclose, and the paid tier's 10 TB is a cap the free tier claims not to have. Expect the free claim to be enforced by account action rather than by a published limit.
confidence_note: Every claim here is the vendor's sentence, read today. None was measured; a 10 GB upload would be the cheapest way to test whether 'no limits on size' survives contact. Until then the record states the claim and says it is a claim.

evidence.proved: the four claims verbatim: free unlimited storage, endless bandwidth at no charge, videos never expire, unlimited uploads with no size or length limit; plus the premium tier at EUR 10/month for 10 TB
there is no /premium route (404 'Not Found'), so the paid terms are only those summarised on the homepage

extras.ad_free: explicitly ad-free even for free users, which is unusual for the video-host model and is the reason the bandwidth claim is worth testing
